note.note:
History:
- Main complaint: Worsening, very itchy, sore, red rash consistent with eczema flare.
- Onset/duration: Began “past few days,” progressively worsening.
- Distribution: Chest, hands, arms, especially bilateral antecubital fossae (inside elbows).
- Character: Dry, cracked skin; no weeping/exudate; no scratch marks or lichenification noted.
- Associated symptoms: Intense pruritus; denies fever, joint pain, or systemic symptoms. Asthma stable.
- Previous episodes: Long-standing eczema, usually controlled with emollients and OTC hydrocortisone; current flare judged “way worse.”

Past Medical History:
- Chronic eczema.
- Asthma (uses blue SABA inhaler PRN).
- Allergies: Denies drug allergies.
- Family history: Mother with migraine and hypothyroidism (doctor repeated “hyperthyroidism” – conflict noted).
- Current medications:
  • Diprobase cream – topical emollient (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  • Dermol shower emollient – topical (frequency not documented).  
  • Hydrocortisone cream – OTC topical steroid (dose/frequency not documented).  
  • Salbutamol “blue” inhaler PRN for asthma (dose/frequency not documented).  
  • No regular antihistamine; previously tried OTC cetirizine without benefit.

Physical Examination:
- Reported widespread erythematous, dry, cracked patches over chest, hands, arms, antecubital fossae.
- No weeping, exudate, or signs of infection.
- No skin thickening or hyperpigmentation.
- Afebrile by history; no joint swelling; breathing comfortable.
- Alert, oriented; conversation coherent.

Impression:
- Acute widespread flare of atopic eczema.

Management Plan:
- Prescribed Fexofenadine (oral antihistamine; dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Prescribed Betnovate (betamethasone valerate) topical steroid: apply thin layer (≈ one fingertip unit) twice daily for 2 weeks.
- Continue current emollients (Diprobase, Dermol).
- Prescription sent electronically to patient’s nominated Boots pharmacy.
- Return sooner if symptoms worsen or any adverse reaction occurs; otherwise review if not improved after 2 weeks.

Patient Summary:
Adult with chronic eczema presents with a several-day widespread pruritic flare on chest and upper limbs. No signs of infection. Started stronger topical steroid and oral antihistamine; instructed to continue regular emollients and seek review if no improvement.

Key Takeaways:
- Apply Betnovate thinly to affected areas twice daily for 14 days.
- Take Fexofenadine as prescribed to reduce itch.
- Maintain regular use of Diprobase and Dermol; seek care if rash worsens or shows signs of infection.

Next Steps:
- Monitor response over the next 2 weeks; contact service earlier if deterioration or no relief.
- If inadequate control, follow-up consultation for possible escalation or dermatology referral.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing elements: vitals, full medication list with doses, thorough review of systems.  
● Conflicts: Patient stated mother has hypothyroidism; doctor repeated “hyperthyroidism” (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor background wording discrepancies but clinically adequate.
